rationales.1: The no-motion renders carry the full three-step story, every caveated figure, and the complete specs/price blocks with nothing hidden or truncated. The static rings even encode step-progress on their own, so a reduced-motion visit reads as a complete object, not a stripped fallback.
rationales.2: The subhead names the product and audience within the same first viewport, but the giant headline 'Three counts: bag, unfold, water' is abstract enough that it takes the second line to know this is a kayak at all.
rationales.3: The setup-time, pack-volume, and load-rating caveats appear twice — inline in the hero copy and again beside each figure in specs — so the honesty framing is unmissable rather than merely present.
rationales.4: The skip control is styled as the bolder, solid-color button next to the outlined 'Play' button, which puts pacing control in the visitor's hand before they've committed to anything.
rationales.5: Spacing and the olive/lime accent are held consistently across light and dark, and the three-step grid reads as one calm system rather than an assembled page.
rationales.6: Payload and JS are the smallest of the three and LCP is comfortably fast, though desktop frame time (17.1ms) is the furthest of the three past the 16.7ms budget, a small but real miss.
rationales.7: The declared device — a running numeric readout instead of a hero image — is honest and clever, but as captured it reads closer to an abstract progress dial than a literal bag-to-hull-to-water demonstration. The scroll-linked motion is confirmed real at runtime; the captures just don't visually settle what it depicts.
rationales.8: Both declared breaks (clock-as-ornament, jump-link specs) are exactly what's on screen, and the surrounding chrome — nav, buttons, CTA — stays completely conventional.
rationales.9: The clock/count framing and lines like 'the clock runs beside them' are specific to this claim and this boat, with no stock launch-page hype language.
rationales.10: Explicit 'Specs' and 'Price' jump links in the nav, on top of the gated second-visit price bypass, make this the most direct return path of the three.
